The organization reported <cite id="2">$15,472,301 in total revenue</cite> in FY2023, though it experienced a <cite id="3">revenue decline to $14,190,451</cite> in FY2024. Despite this recent dip, the foundation maintains an exceptionally lean financial model. Hidaya's model prioritizes direct service delivery, reaching <cite id="7">300,000 beneficiaries</cite> with a low average cost of <cite id="8">$45.44 per person</cite>. Their work spans five core pillars: education, social welfare, environment, health care, and self-employment. For Muslim donors, the foundation offers a <cite id="9">verified zakat program</cite> that covers all <cite id="10">eight asnaf categories</cite>, including the poor and needy.
